title: DbDataBuild command output (--format json)
description: The one JSON document a command writes to standard output with `--format json`. `data` holds what the command found or did, and its shape is checked per command below (`$defs.data_<command>`): keys are present when the command got far enough to produce them (a command refused early has few or none), and null values are omitted rather than written as null. `diagnostics` are the structured form of what text mode prints on standard error; `messages` and `errors` keep the human text so nothing is lost. Exit codes are the same as in text mode: 0 ok, 1 findings, 2 usage, 3 not implemented, 70 internal error. Metadata documents (`project compile`, `project show metadata`) are defined in metadata.schema.json (id urn:dbdatabuild:schemas:metadata).

next.description: What to do next, as commands (the `Next:` block of the text). Present when the command has a suggestion.

data_project_compile.description: validation (counts, config, and the metadata when it is clean), then what the compile did: --content: files (with text) and operations; default: files, wrote, removed; --check: files, out_of_date. A project that does not validate stops there.

by_kind.description: The models counted by model kind, all seven kinds (0 for a kind the project has none of).

fields.description: The fields of a dialect profile under `dialects:`.

built_in.description: The built-in dialects, as the tool has them.

types.description: How many catalog type names the dialect maps.

keywords.description: The closed classes of the keywords of a connection's `engine`.

example.description: A project's dialects and connections for a proxy in front of several systems.

connections.description: The connections the metadata of mapped models and copy origins was read from, or why one was skipped.

mapped_models.description: The mapped models (and the tables copies read) compared with their tables: what differs, per model.

catalog_notes.description: What an origin's catalog could not say (indexes where it has no way to, keys a driver does not offer), once each.

online.description: False with --offline: no connection was read.

summary.description: The landing view: structure (in_sync, pending or attention), the newest deploy and refresh event, and the policy in force.

plans.description: One entry per refresh plan compiled for the connection: its last run and how it ended.

data_connection_deploy.description: the plan (questions, plan, files), or the apply of one (outcomes, statements), or an acknowledgement, by the option given.

check.description: The safety check that ran before the loads.

parallel.description: How many loads ran at once at most: the flag, else the plan's setting, else 1, capped by the destination's max_parallel (1 in a dry run).

parallel_effective.description: How many loads ran at once at most in the end: `parallel`, or 1 when it was above 1 and the loads file carries no dependency graph (compiled by an older version: the loads then run in plan order, and `warnings` says so).

loads.description: The loads of the plan that were selected, in the order they run, with the inputs each runs with.

source.description: flag, membership, parameter, resolver:target or initial (resolver before the load runs)

findings.description: The codes of what the check found.

plan.description: The refresh plan that ran; null for loads named directly.

plan_hash.description: The hash of the plan's file (for loads named directly, of their load plans).

selection.description: The selectors given after the plan; null when the whole plan ran.

plans.description: When no plan could be chosen: the plans compiled for the connection.

outcome.description: How the run ended: completed, completed_with_failures (some loads failed or were skipped), stopped (a load failed under on_failure stop, or the operator stopped it) or failed (nothing was done).

results.description: Every load of the run and how it ended.

state.description: done, failed, skipped or not run

reason.description: Why it failed or was skipped: check, max runtime, busy, input, upstream failed, stopped, check failed; null otherwise.

status.description: The text run_log records: ok, failed, failed: <kind>, skipped: <reason> or not run.

note.description: upstream skipped: busy, on a load that ran although a load it reads was skipped because it was busy.

warnings.description: Failures that on_failure: ignore let pass.

last_run.description: With --only-failed: the event whose loads were repeated.

plan.description: With a plan named: its runs, the last complete run and the last partial one apart, and each member's last success and failure.

kind.description: The model kind of the table: a built kind for a result, `mapped` or `native` for a declared model that was filled.

dependencies.description: The rows of the tracking table metadata_dependency: how many the project has, and for how many models (and native models) this publish wrote them again because they differed from the stored ones.

online.description: False with --offline: no connection was read.

differences.description: With --check: how many things would change (definitions out of step with their queries, mapped models that differ from their tables, dialects that are new or changed).

definitions.description: The definitions of the models, from their queries (what project model update does).

dialects.description: One row per connection in scope: the dialect a Flight SQL server reports, or why none was asked.

connections.description: The connections the metadata of mapped models and copy origins was read from, or why one was skipped.

mapped_models.description: The mapped models (and the tables copies read) compared with their tables: what differs, per model.

catalog_notes.description: What an origin's catalog could not say (indexes where it has no way to, keys a driver does not offer), once each.
What the origin's catalog could not say (indexes where it has no way to, keys a driver does not offer), once each.

rows.description: The first violating rows (--limit), each an object of the rule's columns.

category.description: What the node is: a model of the project (any of the seven kinds; `kind` says which), a macro, or a table that is none of the project's.

kind.description: The model kind of a model node; absent for a macro or an unknown table.

against_connection.description: The connection of the right-hand table when it is not the left one's; the comparison is then by digests computed in each engine.

partial.description: Across connections only: so many rows differ that the comparison stopped at the buckets of the key. The counts above are then not known; this says how many buckets differ, how many rows they hold and which columns differ.

samples.description: Present only with --show-values: real values, in the output the operator asked for.

additionalProperties.description: A side that is NULL is left out.

data_project_show_plan.description: no plan: plans; a plan file: path, intact, plan, report, risky, destructive, apply_needs (a plan that does not parse: path and intact false).

load_members.description: Only when a plan is named: its members in the order they run.

waits_for.description: What this member's model waits for among the models of the plan, from the dependency graph in loads.yml: the model, its model kind and how many steps away (1 is direct). Null when the loads file carries no graph.

dependencies.description: The dependency graph loads.yml carries, among the models of this plan: one edge per model and thing it waits for, direct (depth 1) and through others, with the model kind of each side. Null when the loads file carries no graph (compiled by an older version).

data_project_show_refresh.description: The compiled refresh plans: one entry per plan and connection.

plan_health.description: Whether a plan keeps to its expected_every: overdue (its last run began longer ago than that, or it never ran) and slow (its last run took longer than that, with the slowest load named). All fields are null or false when the plan declares no expected_every.
